title: Flame Color Test Chemistry Lab
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D chemistry lab flame color test simulation using Three.js and GLTFLoader (from CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.163.0/). Load TWO 3D assets: 'Xbot.glb' as the lab technician character standing behind the lab bench, and 'horse.glb' as a decorative lab mascot statue placed on a shelf in the background. Both must be loaded via GLTFLoader and visible in the scene.

SCENE SETUP:
- A dark chemistry lab environment with a lab bench (box geometry, dark grey) centered in the scene.
- A Bunsen burner on the bench (cylinder geometry, metallic grey, height ~0.3 units) at position (0, benchTopY, 0).
- The Bunsen burner has a flame (cone geometry) above it that changes color based on the active metal salt sample.
- Three sample dishes on the bench to the left of the burner, each a small cylinder with colored material: Sodium (white-ish, label 'Na'), Potassium (white-ish, label 'K'), Copper (blue-green-ish, label 'Cu').
- Xbot.glb loaded at position (-2, 0, -1), scaled to ~0.8, facing the bench. Play idle animation if available.
- horse.glb loaded at position (3, 1.5, -3), scaled to ~0.5, placed on a shelf (box geometry) as a decorative mascot.
- Camera at (0, 3, 5) looking at the bench. OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.15) and a point light above the burner that changes color with the flame.

METAL SALT SAMPLES & FLAME COLORS:
- Sodium (Na): flame color RGB (255, 210, 0) - bright yellow, flame temperature label '1150°C'
- Potassium (K): flame color RGB (180, 80, 255) - violet/purple, flame temperature label '1032°C'
- Copper (Cu): flame color RGB (50, 220, 100) - green, flame temperature label '1085°C'
- No sample selected: flame color RGB (80, 120, 255) - blue base flame, label 'No sample'

INTERACTIONS:
1. Click on a sample dish (raycasting) to pick it up. The selected sample name appears in the HUD. The dish visually highlights (emissive glow).
2. Press SPACE to introduce the selected sample into the flame. The flame color transitions smoothly (lerp over 0.5s) to the corresponding color. The point light color also changes. A particle system (small spheres or sprites) emits from the flame tip in the flame color.
3. Press 'R' to reset/remove the current sample from the flame. Flame returns to blue base color over 0.5s. Particle emission stops.
4. Press 'T' to toggle the Bunsen burner ON/OFF. When OFF, flame geometry is hidden, no particles, point light intensity = 0. When ON, flame reappears.
5. Press 'U' to UNDO the last action (supports undoing sample introduction and burner toggle, up to 3 levels).
6. DOM buttons: 'Na', 'K', 'Cu' buttons as alternative to clicking dishes. A 'Record Observation' button that logs the current flame color name to an observation list displayed in the HUD.
7. Press keys '1', '2', '3' to directly select Na, K, Cu samples respectively.

HUD/UI:
- Top-left: current sample name, flame temperature, burner status (ON/OFF)
- Top-right: observation log (list of recorded observations, max 10)
- Bottom: three DOM buttons for Na, K, Cu sample selection, plus 'Record Observation' button, plus 'Reset All' button
- The 'Reset All' button clears observations, resets flame to blue, deselects sample, turns burner ON.

STATE MANAGEMENT - expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- burnerOn: boolean
- selectedSample: string ('none', 'Na', 'K', 'Cu')
- flameIntroduced: boolean (whether sample is actively in flame)
- flameColorR, flameColorG, flameColorB: current flame color (0-255 integers, updated each frame)
- flameTemperature: string label
- particlesActive: boolean
- particleCount: number of active particles
- observationLog: array of strings
- observationCount: number
- undoStackSize: number (0-3)
- xbotLoaded: boolean
- horseLoaded: boolean
- modelsLoaded: number (count of loaded GLB models, should be 2)
- pointLightIntensity: number
- pointLightColorR, pointLightColorG, pointLightColorB: 0-255
- lastAction: string describing last action performed
- flameVisible: boolean
- sampleDishCount: number (should be 3)
- transitionProgress: number 0.0-1.0 (1.0 = transition complete)

PHYSICS/VISUAL CONSTRAINTS:
- Flame color lerp must complete in ~0.5 seconds (30 frames at 60fps).
- Point light color must always match flame color within tolerance of 5 per channel.
- Particles must only be active when flameIntroduced === true AND burnerOn === true.
- Turning burner off while sample is introduced should stop particles but remember the sample (turning back on resumes).
- Undo stack must correctly restore previous state.
- All color values must be valid (0-255, no NaN).
physics_constraints: Flame color must lerp smoothly between states over 0.5s. Point light color must synchronize with flame color within ±5 per RGB channel. Particles active only when burner is ON and sample is introduced. Undo stack preserves up to 3 previous states and correctly restores them. All RGB values must remain in [0,255] and be NaN-free. Observation log is append-only until reset.
